inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, post-buyback: paid-up capital Rs19,810m / Rs2 par = 9,905m shares at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27 consolidated balance sheet), plus ~30m dilutive RSUs/options (FY26 basic EPS 12.60 vs diluted 12.56 = 0.3%). The Q2 FY27 weighted diluted count implied by profit/EPS is 9,909m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 finance and other income was Rs36,491m, but Wipro's IFRS cash flow statement removes it from operating activities ('Finance and other income, net of finance costs' is reversed in the OCF reconciliation; 'Interest received' and 'Dividend received' sit in investing; interest paid sits in financing). Reported OCF and FCF are therefore already free of treasury income, so nothing further is stripped - deducting it again would charge it twice. The matching assets (cash, current and non-current investments) are in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated IFRS cash flow add-back 'Share-based compensation expense' (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp 4,465). Equity-award withholding taxes: none disclosed (kpis EquityAwardTaxes = 0); awards are settled by fresh issue / the employee trust, not net-share settlement.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: last_fcf = reported_fcf 133,713 (OCF 149,316 - capex 15,603) - SBC 4,465 - lease payments incl. interest 11,561 (financing activities, FY26 consolidated cash flow) - interest income 0 (already outside OCF). The lease deduction is why last_fcf is not simply reported_fcf - sbc.
inputs.buyback_note: Rs150,508m paid in H1 FY27 (600m shares tendered at Rs250, settled 24 Jun 2026, incl. Rs508m costs). Prior buybacks: FY24 Rs145,173m, FY21 Rs116,644m, FY20 Rs105,311m, FY18 Rs110,312m. A funded repurchaser: buybacks run at ~30x annual SBC, so the flat count is paid for many times over. FY26 itself had no buyback.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z (15:28 IST, NSE regular session, final minutes before the Friday close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows: India 10-year G-sec ~6.6% + beta ~0.75 (large-cap IT exporter, net cash) x 6.5% India equity risk premium (mature-market ERP plus country spread) = ~11.5% cost of equity. Borrowings are short-dated working-capital/treasury lines against 2.4x their value in cash and investments, so WACC is set equal to the cost of equity. One WACC for all three scenarios: GenAI and demand risk is charged in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. Terminal growth 4.5% base is INR-nominal (roughly 2% constant-currency growth plus ~2.5% long-run INR depreciation on a mostly USD/EUR/GBP revenue base), well under the risk-free rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. 'Payment of lease liabilities including interest' (Rs11,561m FY26, 1.25% of revenue; Rs6,226m H1 FY27, 1.26%) is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (Rs36,044m at 30 Sep 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is loans, borrowings and bank overdrafts only. D&A in the tax build is ex right-of-use depreciation (~Rs9,600m, approximated by lease principal: payments 11,561 less lease interest 1,956).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI is immaterial (profit share Rs681m FY26, Rs34m H1 FY27 after Rs2,851m of NCI shares were bought in). Deducted once, at book (Rs1,721m), in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (INR-built WACC, single lease treatment, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule). Wipro is an IT-services operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; not a bank, REIT or holdco. First valuation of this ticker (fresh build, no reconciliation). ANCHORS: FY0 flows are FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026); the balance sheet and share count are 30 Sep 2026, i.e. after the Rs150.5bn buyback and the Rs33bn Mindsprint acquisition (closed 15 May 2026) both left the cash pile. Using a September balance sheet against FY27 as forecast year 1 counts H1 FY27 cash generation (~Rs70bn owner FCF, largely already paid out as buyback and dividend) in both places, while end-of-year discounting from a valuation date 7.5 months into the year over-discounts every flow by about the same amount; the two roughly offset and neither is adjusted. NET CASH: cash 95,016 + current investments 341,527 = 436,543 less borrowings 185,021 = net cash 251,522 (Rs25/share); non-current investments 27,727 and equity-accounted investments 2,228 are added in the equity bridge. Not adjusted: Rs45bn non-current and Rs63bn current tax liabilities (disputed/deferred assessments; see cash-tax path). MARGIN DEFINITION: ebitda_margin_path is IFRS-16 EBITDA plus SBC, i.e. before SBC and before lease cost (FY26 19.95%, H1 FY27 20.03%); the engine then deducts SBC, lease payments and ex-ROU D&A to reach an EBIT of ~16% that ties to reported operating margin (16.3% FY26, 16.2% H1 FY27) less ~0.2pp of lease interest. CASH TAX: cash taxes paid have run well under the P&L charge for years (FY26 paid 26,245 vs expense 40,767; ETR 23.7%), with the difference accumulating as tax liabilities; the model does not capitalise that deferral and ramps the rate on operating EBIT from 23% to 24.5%. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables plus unbilled revenue (~Rs233bn) far exceed payables and contract liabilities, so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -12%. M&A: growth paths are organic plus currency plus the Mindsprint consolidation in year 1 only; further acquisitions are neither in growth nor charged. SBC is small (0.4-0.5% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow but not collapsed. DATA GAP: no outlook/guidance paragraphs were extractable from the OCR'd filings; guidance is taken from the Analysis JSON (Q3 FY27 IT services revenue $2,571-2,625m, -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ cc).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: blend of 3-year equity CAGR (4.26%) and 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (4.85%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year equity CAGR (9.87%) diverges by more than 30% from both the 3-year revenue CAGR (0.78%) and the 5-year EPS CAGR (5.67%), and the 5-year revenue CAGR (8.38%) is inflated by the FY22 Capco acquisition and INR depreciation. Equity is also distorted by Rs150bn-scale buybacks every 2-3 years (the next one, June 2026, cut equity ~10% after FY0). The equity-CAGR default was therefore not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = OCF - capex - SBC - lease payments incl. interest (FY21 117,003; FY23 102,087; FY26 117,687); interest income is not in OCF for this filer so no interest strip applies to any year. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are nearly identical because SBC is under 0.5% of revenue. FY21 was a working-capital-flattered peak (FCF 127,973 on 619bn revenue), which is why the 5-year FCF CAGR is ~zero while revenue grew 50%: owner-FCF margin has fallen from 18.9% to 12.7%. EPS is restated for the 1:1 bonus of December 2024.

base.growth_note: Year 1 (FY27): H1 FY27 revenue Rs492.3bn is +9.8% YoY in INR on ~+0.6% constant currency, the balance being INR depreciation (guidance assumes USD/INR 95.76) and Mindsprint from 15 May 2026; Q3 guided -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ cc, so FY27 lands near Rs987bn. Later years: 2-2.5% constant-currency growth plus ~2.5% INR depreciation.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-lease EBITDA margin held at ~20% (FY26 19.95%, H1 FY27 20.03%), with a small dip in FY28-29 for the AI/engineering investment management says it will make at the expense of near-term margin. D&A (ex-ROU) starts elevated on Mindsprint intangibles and fades to the FY26 level; capex drifts up to equal D&A by the terminal year so the terminal flow is not flattered by under-investment.

scenario_narratives.base: Wipro stays what it has been for a decade: the slowest-growing of India's big four, with constant-currency growth of about 2% a year and reported INR growth of 4.5-5% once rupee depreciation is added. GenAI takes price out of legacy run-and-maintain work at roughly the rate that AI-led transformation, GCC build-outs and Capco consulting add new work, so volume is flat to slightly up and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin sits at ~20% (operating margin ~16-16.5%, where it has been since FY23). The soft Q2 FY27 bookings (large-deal TCV -58.6% QoQ) are treated as half timing, half real: FY28 growth dips to 4% before the Olam-type deals ramp. Owner-FCF margin settles near 11.5-12%, a little below FY26's 12.7% because cash taxes catch up with the P&L charge and growing receivables absorb cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: The consulting-led, AI-powered repositioning works. Wipro Intelligence and the Capco/Designit/Mindsprint front end win a steady flow of $500m+ transformation deals, the BFSI budget cycle turns (34.5% of revenue), and Wipro closes the growth gap to Infosys and HCLTech: 4-5% constant-currency growth, 7-8% in INR. AI productivity is partly retained rather than passed through as discounts, lifting the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 20% to 21.5% (operating margin ~18%, the level last seen in FY21-22), and a more offshore, less office-bound delivery mix trims lease cost. This needs demand, pricing power and execution to go right together at a company that has missed on all three before.
scenario_narratives.bear: GenAI does to labour arbitrage what the brokerage estimates warn of: 10-15% of revenue is deflated out of application maintenance, testing and BPS over FY28-30 as clients demand AI-productivity discounts and insource through their own GCCs. Bookings weakness proves to be demand, not paperwork; constant-currency revenue shrinks 2-3.5% a year for three years, leaving INR revenue flat even with rupee depreciation, and recovers only to ~0.5-1% real growth. Pricing concessions arrive faster than headcount can be cut, so the pre-SBC EBITDA margin falls three points to 17% (operating margin ~12.5-13%), and lease and capex ratios rise on a stalled revenue base. The business still generates ~Rs80-90bn a year of owner FCF throughout - the terminal value does not approach the zero floor - but it is capitalised at 12x as an ex-growth services firm.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the threat is structural (GenAI compressing the offshore labour-arbitrage model that underpins 62% of revenue), the leading indicators point that way (bookings -22.9% QoQ, large-deal TCV -58.6% QoQ, Q3 guide flat-to-down), and Wipro enters as the peer-group laggard; it is not higher because the balance sheet carries Rs250bn of net cash and no solvency path exists. Base 50%: a continuation of the FY23-FY27 pattern of ~flat constant-currency revenue and a stable ~16% operating margin. Bull cut to 25%: it needs a demand recovery, retained AI productivity and share gains simultaneously, at a company that has under-delivered against TCS, Infosys and HCLTech for years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Wipro is valued as a mature, cash-generative, slow-growing IT-services franchise: about Rs117bn of owner free cash flow (after SBC and lease payments, before any treasury income) on Rs926bn of revenue, plus roughly Rs280bn of net cash and investments left after the June 2026 buyback. Almost all of the valuation question is whether GenAI erodes the labour-arbitrage revenue base faster than AI-led work replaces it; that risk is carried in three explicit revenue-and-margin paths and a 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate. Flows are discounted at an INR-built 11.5%, and the terminal value is the lower of Gordon growth and a 12-17x cap.
key_risks_to_valuation: GenAI price deflation in run/maintain and BPS work: each 1pt of sustained EBITDA margin is worth roughly 5% of enterprise value, and the bear path assumes three
Bookings: Q2 FY27 large-deal TCV fell 58.6% QoQ; if the deferred signings do not close in Q3 FY27 the base FY28 growth of 4% is too high

Currency: every flow is INR-nominal on a USD/EUR/GBP revenue base; the 4.5% terminal growth embeds ~2.5%/yr rupee depreciation, and a stable or appreciating rupee would cut reported growth to the ~2% constant-currency rate
Cash tax: taxes paid have run ~Rs14bn a year below the P&L charge, building Rs109bn of current and non-current tax liabilities; an adverse settlement is a direct deduction not in the bridge
Capital allocation: Rs33bn went on Mindsprint in H1 FY27 and serial acquisitions (Capco, Designit, Mindsprint) are not charged as a recurring cost; goodwill is Rs409bn, half of equity
Balance-sheet vintage: net cash is as of 30 Sep 2026 while FY0 flows are the year to March 2026
